findings.text: A table of filter virtual machine conformance vectors provides named programs plus expected outcomes for an in kernel self test harness, covering both classic accumulator programs and newer register based internal programs.

Each vector conceptually carries a label, an instruction sequence in one of two encodings, a mode marker, flag bits for special handling, associated data and expected result pairs, and optionally a fill callback plus an expected error code.

Classic scratch storage offers sixteen word cells addressed zero through fifteen, writable from the index register and readable back into arithmetic, with one vector filling every cell then accumulating their sum.

Classic execution centers on accumulator and index registers with load, store, exchange, arithmetic and return operations, while internal execution uses general registers with register zero as the result carrier and an explicit terminating operation.

Thirty two bit operations confine their result to the low half and clear the upper half, whereas sixty four bit immediate moves preserve signedness so negative sources appear sign extended when the high half is later observed.

Sign extending moves propagate the sign of an eight, sixteen or thirty two bit source into a wider destination, with the thirty two bit form yielding a zero padded upper half and the sixty four bit form extending across the full width.

Addition, subtraction and multiplication wrap modulo the operation width, so thirty two bit overflow discards carry while sixty four bit arithmetic retains the wider result, including checked wide multiply low and high halves.
Full width constants can be materialized in one step and their high and low halves separately verified through shifts and equality checks, including values that do not fit in thirty two bits.

Internal test programs follow an initialize, compute, compare and exit flow where registers are seeded, the operation under test runs, an equality branch selects a success return code versus a failure return code, and execution terminates.

Expected outcomes pair a case selector with an anticipated numeric return, used both for direct value checks and for boolean pass markers where one value denotes agreement and another denotes the mismatch path.

Ancillary data addressing has an upper bound derived from a base offset and a maximum count; a word load at base plus maximum is rejected during checking with an invalid argument error, establishing that address as out of range.

Successful validation does not guarantee runtime success: a load just below the ancillary base passes the checker yet produces zero at runtime rather than the requested constant, so callers must tolerate runtime failure after acceptance.
